desc:
prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You may make as many transactions as you like; a transaction is one purchase of a single share followed by a sale. You can hold at most one share at a time, and you may sell and buy again on the same day.

A share must be kept for at least h days: if you buy on day b, the earliest day you may sell it is b + h. Return the maximum total profit (at least 0).

Example: prices = [1,3,2,6,4,8]. With h = 1 the answer is 10 (2 + 4 + 4). With h = 3 it is 7 (buy at 1, sell at 8 on day 5). With h = 6 no sale is ever possible, so the answer is 0.
hints: Let f[i] be the best profit achievable using days up to i with nothing held at the end of day i. How does a sale on day i look?
If you sell on day i, the share was bought on some day j ≤ i - h, and before that purchase you had earned f[j]. So the sale yields prices[i] + f[j] - prices[j].
f[i] = max(f[i-1], prices[i] + best[i-h]) where best[k] = max over j ≤ k of (f[j] - prices[j]), a running maximum. For i < h only f[i-1] is possible.
editorial: Define f[i] as the maximum profit after day i with no share in hand. Either nothing happens on day i (f[i-1]), or a share is sold on day i. That share was bought on some day j with j + h ≤ i, and just before buying you were flat having earned at most f[j] (a sale on day j itself is fine). The total is f[j] - prices[j] + prices[i].

Maximising over all admissible j means maximising g[j] = f[j] - prices[j] over the prefix j ≤ i - h. Keep the prefix maxima best[k] in an array: when processing day i, f[i-1] and best[i-h] are both already known, and afterwards g[i] extends the running maximum.
Total time O(n), memory O(n). For h = 1 the formula collapses to the classic unlimited-transactions answer (sum of all rises).
solution:
def maxProfitMinHold(prices, h):
    n = len(prices)
    f = [0] * n
    best = [0] * n
    for i in range(n):
        f[i] = f[i - 1] if i else 0
        if i >= h:
            f[i] = max(f[i], prices[i] + best[i - h])
        g = f[i] - prices[i]
        best[i] = max(best[i - 1], g) if i else g
    return f[n - 1]
